pr.title: Leave from CopyProp early when there are no replacements
pr.author: tmiasko

processing.reason: The PR is a performance optimization with no semantic change. The historical path only omitted the early return when `any_replacement` was false; in that case `Replacer` has an identity copy-class map, so it performs no replacements, and the old code already skipped `remove_unused_definitions`. The patched path merely returns before that no-op rewrite. When `any_replacement` is true, both versions run fully-moved analysis, the Replacer, and `remove_unused_definitions`. Changing the `DenseBitSet` allocation domain from `fully_moved.domain_size()` to `body.local_decls.len()` also cannot affect observable semantics, only capacity. Therefore the only justified "wrong transformation" is extra work on identity copy-class bodies, which has no differing runtime value or MIR semantic effect to encode as a source-grounded counterexample pair. Manufacturing a value difference would require an arbitrary unrelated rewrite.

evidence: Leave from CopyProp early when there are no replacements
Replacer { tcx, copy_classes: ssa.copy_classes(), fully_moved, storage_to_remove }
analysis.incorrectTransformation: For a body whose copy-class map is entirely trivial (`local == head` for every entry), the historical transformation still computed fully-moved locals and invoked the `Replacer`, even though no local can be replaced. That unnecessary rewrite work is the avoidable transformation; the patch leaves the body untouched in that case. This is an optimization, not evidence that the old pass produced wrong MIR.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies after SSA/copy-class analysis, including bodies with no eliminable copies (identity copy classes) and bodies containing at least one non-trivial copy class. The relevant state is `ssa.copy_classes()`, a mapping whose entries satisfy either `local == head` (no replacement) or `local != head` (replacement candidate).
analysis.originalLogic: The original pass first called `fully_moved_locals(&ssa, body)` unconditionally, allocated `storage_to_remove` using `fully_moved.domain_size()`, and filled it by scanning `ssa.copy_classes()` for `local != head`. It then performed a separate scan, `let any_replacement = ssa.copy_classes().iter_enumerated().any(|(l, &h)| l != h);`, always ran `Replacer { ... }.visit_body_preserves_cfg(body);`, and finally called `crate::simplify::remove_unused_definitions(body)` only under `if any_replacement`.
pitfalls: Do not conflate this performance early-return with a semantic correction: the old path was unconditional work, not a known wrong replacement.
Do not return early merely because `storage_to_remove` is empty without also proving there is no non-trivial copy class; the replacement condition is `local != head`.
The old `storage_to_remove` capacity used `fully_moved.domain_size()`; moving allocation before `fully_moved` exists requires a valid local domain such as `body.local_decls.len()`.
Keep `remove_unused_definitions` on the replacement path; dropping it when `any_replacement` is true would leave dead definitions after propagation.
An early return must not skip required MIR invariants for bodies that actually contain copy classes.
preconditions: Copy classes must already be computed by SSA analysis before deciding whether replacements exist.
The early-exit condition is exactly the absence of any `local != head` entry in `ssa.copy_classes()`.
When at least one such entry exists, fully-moved analysis and `Replacer::visit_body_preserves_cfg` must still run.
`remove_unused_definitions` must still run whenever replacements occurred; only the no-replacement path may skip it.
analysis.summary: CopyProp can skip its entire rewrite pipeline when the SSA copy-class map contains no non-trivial class (no local maps to a different head). The historical implementation always computed fully-moved locals and ran the replacer even in that identity case, then guarded only the final unused-definition cleanup. The PR folds detection of any replacement into the existing copy_classes scan and returns early, while preserving cleanup whenever at least one replacement exists.
analysis.testStrategy: Construct two MIR inputs that differ only in whether an eliminable copy exists: (1) a body with only identity copy classes, which should be left unchanged and exercise the early return; (2) a body with at least one `local != head` copy class, which should still perform replacement and unused-definition cleanup. In Rust test terms, use the MIR optimization test machinery / `-Zdump-mir`-style before-after tests to assert identity inputs are unchanged and copy-bearing inputs still propagate, rather than asserting runtime output. The supplied patch contains no regression test changes.
analysis.trigger: The pass should exit early when no `copy_classes()` entry has `local != head`, i.e. the copy-class map is an identity mapping and `any_replacement` remains false.
